a.summary: The Result-identical routing preamble still advertises a live "singleton-null exception in InstructionRecord" to look for, but the delta deleted that row from the baseline entirely.
a.failure_scenario: A reviewer auditing tx-accepted.csv against README.md reads line 336-338, which introduces the `# result identical routing` family as covering "two branches" plus a separately documented exception in `InstructionRecord`. They grep the CSV for an `InstructionRecord` row to find that exception and get nothing - there is no `InstructionRecord` row of any label left in any accepted CSV in the repo. The pointer now lands, 60 lines later, in a section headed "Retired compatibility acceptances", which records the opposite of what the preamble implies.

b.summary: The rewritten closing clause of the untriaged-debt paragraph no longer qualifies anything and collides with a different set of entries the same section already calls "historical evidence".
b.failure_scenario: A reader reaches the end of "## Untriaged debt (tx suite)" and hits "No other current tx baseline row carries `# untriaged`; the retired entries above are historical evidence." The clause it replaced ("the pending-retirement entries above are recorded separately") was a real caveat: those were current baseline rows carrying a non-`# untriaged` label. Now no such rows exist, so the clause qualifies nothing, and "above" most naturally resolves to the two bullets at lines 559-584 that line 557 already describes as "historical evidence, not retained debt" - a different set from the retired acceptances 200 lines earlier. The reader either reads it as a redundant restatement of line 557 or chases the wrong section.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
